items.summary: Republican redistricting largely backfired in Texas and beyond, but one redrawn district delivered for the party.

items.title: Iraq’s al-Zaidi talks to Trump as Baghdad seeks to stay out of war on Iran
items.summary: Call comes as Iraq's top diplomat urges armed groups not to join any Iranian retaliation to US attacks.

items.summary: Following election losses, the signing marks Trump's third event of the week focused on signature renovation projects.

items.summary: UN says settlers reportedly used live ammunition and beat Palestinians, forcing families to flee for their safety.

items.summary: Nithya Raman's victory in LA marks the second major win for Democratic Socialists in a year.

items.summary: Palestinians in Gaza have made wind turbines to generate electricity, using scraps found in the rubble.

items.summary: Lawmakers have voted to impeach Paraguay’s President Santiago Pena amid a banking collapse that has roiled the country.

items.summary: Putin meets Iran's top security official to discuss regional security and receives a letter from Mojtaba Khamenei.

items.title: Gaza turns discarded cooking pots into seawalls
items.summary: As winter approaches, Palestinians in Gaza are turning damaged cooking pots into makeshift seawalls to avoid flooding.

items.title: California governor commutes sentences of more than 500 people on death row
items.summary: Gavin Newsom cites state values and flaws in the legal system as he grants largest mass clemency in US history.

items.title: Israeli settlers set fire to Palestinian olive grove near Ramallah
items.summary: Israeli settlers have set fire to olive trees belonging to Palestinian farmers in the village of Burqa, near Ramallah.

items.title: Turkiye’s parliament ratifies Mecca defence agreement
items.summary: Parliament's approval lays the groundwork for further Turkish involvement in Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Houthis.

items.title: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal is near after meeting Putin’s envoy
items.summary: Though the US president said deal was 'very close', he gave no specifics and did not meet visiting Ukrainian delegation.

items.title: Iran war live: Trump warns US may have to ‘destroy’ rest of Iran
items.summary: Trump says the US may have to 'destroy' the rest of Iran, adding that people will 'know soon enough'.

items.title: Nithya Raman wins LA mayoral race, becoming city’s first South Asian mayor
items.summary: DSA-backed Raman will lead the second-largest US city, promising action on homelessness and affordable housing.

items.title: Generation Z and young voters help redefine US politics after midterms
items.summary: Melat Kiros becomes the first Generation Z woman elected to Congress, embodying a new era of political representation.

items.title: South Africa’s ANC on track for new lows in local polls
items.summary: The ANC was on about 32 percent of the vote with more than 60 percent of votes counted in municipal elections.

items.title: Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel mourned by family and friends
items.summary: The 30-year-old striker suffered cardiac arrest following an on-field collision.

items.title: Israeli demolitions displace more than 100 Palestinians in Biddu
items.summary: Israeli forces demolished five homes in Biddu, occupied West Bank, displacing more than 100 people.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
items.summary: Bomb threats are causing travel disruptions at airports across Europe, targeting at least 27 flights.

items.title: Saudi coalition intercepts missile fired towards Medina
items.summary: Interception comes after Saudi civil defence agency warned of potential danger near the strategic port of Yanbu.

items.title: Why are wealthy countries failing developing nations?
items.summary: UN report warns climate adaptation funding is falling far short of needs.

items.title: US judge temporarily blocks Trump's arch project after panel approval
items.summary: A judge ordered a two-week stop to construction on US President Trump's arch project in Washington. A federal panel had approved Trump's triumphal arch plans in an 8-4 vote.

items.title: Ex-lawmaker jailed in Macau's first national security trial
items.summary: Pro-democracy former lawmaker Au Kam San was found guilty of "subversion against the political power of the State." He was handed a prison sentence of 12-and-a-half years.

items.title: Asian stocks slump after US tech rout amid AI jitters
items.summary: Concerns that Democrats in the US will push back against data center projects are weighing on an AI trade that is already on shaky footing amid growing doubts about profitability.

items.title: Trump raises prospect of 'big, beautiful' Russia-Ukraine deal
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said the Ukraine war was close to being settled and that ending it might involve "all of Europe." Trump has previously made several similar promises, with no resolution to the conflict in sight.

items.title: Austrian tycoon Rene Benko sentenced to 2 years in prison for fraud
items.summary: Austrian businessman Rene Benko, who suffered a major fall from grace after his real estate empire, Signa Holding, went bust, was handed two more years in prison.

items.title: Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all death row inmates in California
items.summary: Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and a rumored presidential candidate, moved to commute the death sentences of 548 inmates in California for one of his last acts as governor of the state.

items.title: Americans voted against Trump's Iran war. Gulf countries hope that means an end to the conflict
items.summary: The US midterm results showed how unpopular Donald Trump's Iran war is. Now, Gulf countries, trapped for months in the middle of the war between the US and Iran, see reason for optimism.

items.title: Pete Hegseth under fire as Republicans trade blame for midterm debacle
items.summary: Iran war hawk Pete Hegseth is facing the fallout from Republicans' midterms losses as high energy prices turned voters toward Democrats. US President Trump continues to support his embattled defense chief — for now.

items.title: Does the Oleshky ceasefire signal progress to come in Ukraine?
items.summary: Hundreds of civilians were evacuated from the city of Oleshky after Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire. Some observers have expressed optimism that more such humanitarian missions might follow.

items.title: France: More than 600,000 protest as anger grows over cost of living
items.summary: Demonstrators took to the streets in several French cities to call for government action on the high cost of living. Protests were largely peaceful, but there were some reports of escalation, including in Paris.

items.title: Arrests and investigations as Serbia begins post-election clean-up
items.summary: The landslide victory of the Students' List in Serbia's general election seems to have removed a blockage in the justice system: Cases that were long stalled are now suddenly moving forward.

items.title: Germany’s Gen Z protests spark debate on integration, bias
items.summary: Political debate about the recent Gen Z riots have raised the question: Can Germany talk about problems with integration without putting entire groups of people under suspicion?

items.title: Paraguay: President Pena resigns amid bank crisis
items.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Pena has resigned amid a crisis over his ties to collapsed lender Ueno. Millions of customers' accounts are frozen, with public pension and health care funds also tied up.

items.title: British comedian and actor Russell Brand found guilty of rape
items.summary: Prosecutors labeled Brand a sexual predator. He was charged in sexual assault cases spanning from 1999 to 2009.

items.title: Iran signals satisfaction, skepticism after US midterm vote
items.summary: While the Iranian regime says the US midterms will not change Washington's policy toward Tehran, some officials and commentators see the resounding Democratic victory as blowback against the Iran war.

items.title: EU court says CBD foods need approval for sale before they can be certified organic
items.summary: The EU's top court says CBD foods cannot be certified organic without approval for sale. The ruling concerns a cannabis compound whose use in food requires authorization, including before organic certification.

items.title: Who is drug testing Russia's athletes, now that they have returned to international competition?
items.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

items.title: What does Trump's midterm elections loss mean for strained US-India ties?
items.summary: Donald Trump's electoral setback might give New Delhi and Washington space to reset relations, but there is no guarantee that the US will actually change its approach to India.

items.title: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
items.summary: A Jewish academy has opened its doors in Frankfurt. The Central Council of Jews in Germany, the country’s leading Jewish umbrella group, set up the project to combat hate and promote dialogue and learning nationally.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
items.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

items.title: Bomb threats disrupt several flights across Europe
items.summary: At least a dozen flights were either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside Paris and more soon followed.

items.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
items.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

items.title: 36 years later: Hungary opens Communist-era secret service files
items.summary: Decades after the end of Soviet rule, Hungary is releasing all its secret service files. The disclosure is sparking fresh debate about informants, guilt and responsibility.

items.title: The 2011 discovery of neo-Nazi killers aired biases in German policing
items.summary: Many questions still surround the National Socialist Underground whose existence was revealed by neo-Nazi terrorist Beate Zschäpe on November 4, 2011. How has German society reacted to NSU crimes? Has justice been done?

items.title: Kosovo: Outrage as authorities accused of not helping femicide victim
items.summary: Despite reporting her husband to the police and pleading for protection, Arlinda Zekaj was brutally murdered. Now, thousands in Kosovo are protesting what they say is a dramatic failure of state institutions.

items.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
items.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

items.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
items.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

items.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
items.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

items.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
items.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

items.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
items.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

items.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
items.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

items.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
items.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

items.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
items.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

items.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
items.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

items.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
items.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

items.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
items.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

items.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
items.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

items.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
items.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

items.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
items.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

items.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
items.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

items.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
items.summary: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

items.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
items.summary: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

items.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
items.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

items.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
items.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

items.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
items.summary: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

items.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
items.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

items.title: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
items.summary: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

items.title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
items.summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

items.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
items.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

items.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

items.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
items.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

items.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

items.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
items.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

items.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
items.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

items.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
items.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

items.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
items.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

items.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
items.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

items.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
items.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

items.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
items.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

items.title: Germany seeks new head of state
items.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

items.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
items.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

items.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
items.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

items.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
items.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

items.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
items.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

items.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
items.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

items.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
items.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

items.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
items.summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

items.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
items.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

items.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
items.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

items.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
items.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

items.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
items.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

items.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
items.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

items.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
items.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

items.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
items.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

items.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
items.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

items.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
items.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

items.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
items.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

items.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
items.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

items.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
items.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

items.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
items.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

items.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
items.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

items.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
items.summary: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

items.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?
items.summary: Conflicts, rising costs and Chinese competition are testing Germany's economic model like never before. Can new growth sectors create jobs and ease voters' economic fears, thereby helping contain the far-right AfD?

items.title: Germany news: AfD's Weidel calls for major EU reforms
items.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

items.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
items.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

items.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
items.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

items.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
items.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

items.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
items.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

items.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
items.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

items.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
items.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

items.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
items.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

items.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
items.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

items.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
items.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

items.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
items.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

items.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
items.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

items.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
items.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

items.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
items.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

items.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
items.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

items.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
items.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

items.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's PM in a political tangle
items.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
items.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

items.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
items.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.
